name: knobas test estate
description: The real test infrastructure knobas is developed against: this notebook, where `just check` and every live recipe run, and the Windows desktop whose WSL 2 VM holds the Docker engine and the containers testenv/docker-compose.yml runs there -- Gitea, Uptime Kuma and its read-only Docker API, and the real TeamCity, Jira and Confluence, up around the clock since 2026-11-01 (#2366) and reached from the notebook through an ssh tunnel. Data about an estate that exists -- nothing here is invented, and nothing Tidewater-shaped belongs in it. The `monitors` names are the names that Uptime Kuma actually holds, seeded from `monitors.json` (#441). Until 2026-10-12 three Hetzner servers held the JVM products; they were decommissioned (#634) and left this file with them. Until 2026-11-01 the containers ran on demand in a Linux VM on the notebook itself.

assets.name: knobas test estate
assets.description: The root. Environment and owner are set here only; everything below inherits them from the nearest ancestor that sets them (spec §12.1).

assets.name: devs-MacBook-Pro
assets.description: The development notebook, and the machine `just check` and every live recipe run on. Since 2026-11-01 it runs no container: the live products are on the WSL box, and it reaches them through the ssh tunnel `testenv/live tunnel` opens. Typed custom because it holds nothing in this tree any more and the type table has no name for a workstation; `hypervisor` was honest only while it held the Linux VM the containers ran in. Its `ip` is its Tailscale address, the one the `notebook` ping watches from the Uptime Kuma on the WSL box.

assets.name: DESKTOP-QUUAHUB
assets.description: The Windows desktop that runs WSL 2, and with it the live products, 24/7 since 2026-11-01 (#2366). Typed hypervisor because what it holds here is the WSL 2 VM. Set up by `testenv/wsl/setup-windows.ps1` (testenv/README.md, "Live products on a remote machine (WSL)").

assets.name: Ubuntu 26.04 (WSL 2)
assets.description: WSL 2's Ubuntu VM on the desktop, where the Docker engine the live products run in lives. `setup-windows.ps1` gives WSL the physical memory less 6 GB; this box's WSL already had 12 GB. The live products stay up there 24/7 under a memory budget (testenv/README.md, "Live products on a remote machine (WSL)"). Its `ip` is the Docker bridge, what `host.docker.internal` resolves to for its containers; the notebook logs in over ssh as `knobas-wsl`.

assets.name: Docker engine (WSL)
assets.description: The engine `testenv/docker-compose.yml` brings every service up on, reached from the notebook as `DOCKER_HOST=ssh://knobas-wsl` and through the `wsl` docker context `testenv/wsl/connect.sh` creates: Gitea, Uptime Kuma and its Docker API proxy, and the real TeamCity, Jira and Confluence with what each needs.

assets.name: knobas-gitea
assets.description: Gitea: a real product, the Gitea adapter's witness, and the VCS the TeamCity builds clone from over the compose network. Up around the clock on the WSL box: no run stops it when it ends.

assets.name: knobas-forgejo
assets.description: Forgejo, the hard fork of Gitea, run through the same adapter (#1195): `just gitea-live forgejo` starts it, on its own opt-in profile, volume and seed state. On the WSL box no run stops it once it is up, so it is part of what the engine runs.

assets.name: knobas-https-front
assets.description: Caddy, the https front for Gitea (3443) and Forgejo (3445) (#2377): knobas clones over https or ssh only, and the forges serve http. Its certificate comes from its own local CA, which `just live-trust-ca` trusts on the Mac. Up with either forge.

assets.name: knobas-uptime-kuma
assets.description: Uptime Kuma v2: the system of record for every monitor this file names. On the WSL box with the products since 2026-11-01, so the notebook runs no container. It does not watch itself.

assets.name: knobas-docker-proxy
assets.description: Uptime Kuma's read-only Docker API (#978): the Docker host its docker monitors read, holding the engine's socket and passing on only GET /containers/*. It publishes no port and shares an internal network with Kuma alone. Recorded because it runs on the box, and `just estate-live` requires every running container to be in this file.

assets.name: knobas-teamcity
assets.description: The TeamCity server. Up around the clock on the WSL box: no run stops it when it ends, and its volumes keep its builds. Only the memory budget would stop it, for a start that finds no room, and on this box all three products fit.

assets.name: teamcity
assets.description: TeamCity's internal database. There is no database container for it: the engine is embedded in the server, which is what the compose file's comment rules and what `down -v` throws away.

assets.name: knobas-teamcity-agent
assets.description: The one build agent, because a server with none runs nothing. It publishes no port and has no monitor of its own; it starts and stops with its server.

assets.name: knobas-jira
assets.description: Jira Software Data Center 10.3 LTS, on a 10-user, 3-hour timebomb licence. Up around the clock on the WSL box, and no run stops it. When less than an hour of the licence is left, the next run or `live-up` removes it with its volumes and sets it up again from empty.

assets.name: knobas-jira-db
assets.description: Jira's PostgreSQL, set up again from empty with Jira when its licence is due.

assets.name: knobas-confluence
assets.description: Confluence Data Center, the only contract there is for it: Atlassian publishes no machine-readable Confluence DC spec. Up around the clock on the WSL box, and set up again from empty when its licence is due, as Jira is.

assets.name: knobas-confluence-db
assets.description: Confluence's PostgreSQL, set up again from empty with Confluence when its licence is due.
